sections.title: Skill overview
paragraphs: Tornado creates a storm that pulls nearby enemies and deals physical damage over time. It can absorb the debuff from an elemental ground surface it overlaps and add damage of that element.
The base duration is eight seconds and the base limit is one. Quality can extend duration and raise the number of simultaneous Tornadoes.
bullets: Spell damage modifiers apply to its damage-over-time debuff.
The storm has a three-metre radius.
Ground absorption is a major part of elemental variants.

sections.title: Core mechanics
paragraphs: The Tornado itself is a damage-over-time spell rather than a repeated hit engine. Elemental ground changes both the debuff it applies and the extra elemental damage it deals.
Increasing the limit allows multiple storms, while duration determines how long each placement contributes. Do not confuse Tornado with Tornado Shot, which is a different projectile skill.
bullets: Quality can add duration and Tornado limit.

supports.label: Prolonged Duration
notes: Extends storm uptime and reduces recasting pressure.

supports.label: Magnified Area
notes: Improves pull and damage coverage for mapping.

supports.label: Physical Mastery
notes: Raises the level of the physical skill.

sections.title: Build use cases
paragraphs: Use Tornado in Archon trigger chains, physical DoT setups, or elemental-ground combinations that can reliably place the desired surface beneath the storm.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not scale only hit damage: Tornado's core is non-ailment damage over time. Also confirm that the ground surface overlaps the storm instead of assuming any nearby surface is absorbed.

items.question: Can Tornado absorb more than one element?
answer: It can deal extra damage for absorbed elemental ground types; practical setups should verify overlap and uptime for each surface.

items.question: Is Tornado the same as Tornado Shot?
answer: No. Tornado is a spell and damage-over-time storm; Tornado Shot is a separate projectile attack.
